table.title: ফসল মৌসুমভিত্তিক বপন, কর্তন ও ফলন সূচি
table.html:
ফসলবপনকাটাফলন (টন/হেক্টর)মন্তব্য
বোরো ধান (উফশী)ডিসেম্বরের শেষ সপ্তাহ–জানুয়ারির মাঝামাঝিএপ্রিলের শেষ–মে মাসের প্রথম সপ্তাহ৫.৮–৬.৪সেচনির্ভর চাষ; কুয়াশা ও ঠান্ডায় চারা মরে যাওয়ার ঝুঁকি থাকে, তাই পলিথিনে চারা তৈরি করলে জমিতে প্রতিষ্ঠা ভালো হয়। পোকা দমনে সমন্বিত ব্যবস্থাপনা অনুসরণ করতে হবে।
আমন ধান (স্থানীয়)জুনের শেষ–জুলাইয়ের মাঝামাঝিনভেম্বরের মাঝামাঝি–ডিসেম্বরের শুরু৩.২–৩.৮বৃষ্টিনির্ভর চাষ; জমিতে পানি ধরে রাখার ব্যবস্থা থাকলে ফলন স্থিতিশীল হয়। দেরিতে বপন করলে শীতকালীন কুয়াশায় চিটা বাড়ে।
গম (বারি গম-৩৩)নভেম্বরের প্রথম–শেষ সপ্তাহমার্চের প্রথম–তৃতীয় সপ্তাহ৩.৫–৪.২সেচের সময়সূচি ঠিক রাখা জরুরি; বিশেষ করে মুকুল আসার সময় ও দানা গঠনের পর্যায়ে পানি না দিলে ফলন কমে। জমি ভালোভাবে সমান করতে হবে।
সরিষা (বারি সরিষা-১৪)অক্টোবরের শেষ–নভেম্বরের প্রথম সপ্তাহজানুয়ারির শেষ–ফেব্রুয়ারির প্রথম সপ্তাহ১.৪–১.৮কম সেচে চলে; তবে ফুল আসার আগে একবার সেচ দিলে ফলন বাড়ে। জাব পোকা দেখা দিলে দ্রুত ব্যবস্থা নিতে হবে, নইলে ফুল ও কোষ ঝরে যায়।
পাট (তোষা)মার্চের শেষ–এপ্রিলের মাঝামাঝিজুলাইয়ের প্রথম–মধ্য২.৬–৩.১উঁচু ও বৃষ্টিবহুল জমি উপযোগী; বীজ বপনের পর আগাছা দমন না করলে গাছ দুর্বল হয়। আঁশ পচানোর সময় পরিষ্কার পানি ব্যবহার করতে হবে।
মসুর ডালঅক্টোবরের শেষ–নভেম্বরের প্রথমফেব্রুয়ারির শেষ–মার্চের প্রথম১.২–১.৬শুষ্ক মৌসুমে তুলনামূলক নিরাপদ; বীজ বপনের আগে বীজ শোধন করলে গোড়া পচা রোগ কম হয়। পাকা অবস্থায় দেরি করলে শুঁটি ফেটে যাওয়ার ঝুঁকি থাকে।
table.brief: ফসলের মৌসুম: ফসল সারি শিরোনাম, বপন, কাটা, ফলন, মন্তব্য (দীর্ঘ)

understanding.purpose: A crop-by-crop reference table for comparing sowing windows, harvest windows, yield, and notes across crops.
understanding.reading: Readers anchor on the crop name in column 1, compare the paired sowing and harvest windows in columns 2–3, then check the short yield value and read remarks. Rows should remain readable as units, so wrapping in long date phrases and remarks must not make the schedule hard to scan.
groups: Columns 2–3: বপন and কাটা are the paired temporal comparison and should have related widths and rhythm.
Columns 4–5: both are outcomes after the schedule, but column 4 is a short numeric value while column 5 is long free text, so they should not share a width.
keep_intact: Crop names and parenthetical variety identifiers such as বোরো ধান (উফশী)
Individual Bengali words; never break mid-word
Numeric yield values and the unit টন/হেক্টর
may_wrap: Multiword sowing and harvest date windows at spaces
Crop labels only between words, not inside a word

preferred.name: r3A
preferred.note: Shift 10px from crop to remarks. Crop still has 74px of text, above the 61px longest crop token, and schedule 100/95 plus yield 85 stay at the proven three-line and numeric thresholds. This is the safe refinement of r2C: it relieves the long prose column without disturbing the schedule rhythm, at the cost of allowing one short crop label to wrap.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Push width to remarks to shorten the table: col 5 gets 234, col 1 gets 105, col 4 gets 85; the date columns shrink to 100/95 but remain above the longest-word limit. This tests whether fewer remark lines outweigh tighter date columns.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Keep the strong 105px crop anchor and fund remarks by tightening the paired schedule to 95/90 instead of shrinking the row header; yield stays 85. This tests whether the date windows can absorb a 5px cut without gaining a fourth line, preserving crop identity while giving the prose more measure.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: A more aggressive remarks-first rebalance: crop 95, paired schedule 96/91, yield 80, remarks 257. All columns stay above their unbreakable-word minima. The aim is to bring the five-line first remark down to four lines and even out row heights. Trade-off: the schedule is tighter, so watch for a fourth date line in the longest windows.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Widen col 1 to 100 and col 4 to 85; take 14/15px from the date pair and 6px from remarks. This keeps r1C's compact remarks, gives yield values and the unit header room, and lets crop labels wrap at word boundaries with less crowding.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Protect the sowing/harvest comparison: keep 120/110 for cols 2–3, fix col 4 at 85, and let remarks take the remaining 209. This trades some remark height for clearer date windows.

bad.name: r1B
bad.note: Prioritise the row anchor: 110px lets 'সরিষা (বারি সরিষা-১৪)' and 'বোরো ধান (উফশী)' read as clean two-line labels with the parenthetical intact, which is how readers find a row. Dates stay tight at 125/118 and remarks keeps a workable 206px.
bad.why: The 60px yield column breaks numeric ranges such as ৭.৮–৮.৪ across lines, making one value look like two; the narrow remarks column also forces a very tall, uneven table.

bad.name: r1C
bad.note: Stay close to r0C's winning proportions but rebalance the slack: crop column up from 85 to 90 to clear the 61px longest word with margin, date columns slightly up (126/120) to avoid four-line date cells, yield column held at 60 so '৫.৮–৬.৪' and the টন/হেক্টর unit stay safe, and all of it paid for from remarks, still the widest column at 223px.
bad.why: Same core fault: the 60px yield column splits numeric ranges and forces a three-line header, while excess width sits in the date columns.

rationale: r3A is the most efficient compact layout: crop names still fit in two lines at 95px, the Bengali date ranges remain readable at 100/95px, and the 85px yield column keeps values like ৭.৮–৮.৪ intact. Giving the remaining slack to মন্তব্য at 244px keeps the long prose from dominating row height; the table stays 636px tall with no mid-word splits. r2C is nearly as good but spends 10px more on crop names that do not gain a line, while r3C and r3B tighten the date columns unnecessarily. r1B and r1C fail because their 60px yield column sacrifices the integrity of the numeric data.

general: Keep numeric ranges and identifiers unbroken; a column must be at least as wide as its longest atomic token plus padding.
Allocate width by wrapping cost, not equality: short date columns need enough to avoid fragmentation, while the long prose column should receive remaining slack.
A row-header column needs enough width for graceful two-line labels, not necessarily the widest column in the table.
A two-line header is usually acceptable if it protects the data values; a three-line header that forces numeric values to split is not.
specific: Bengali crop-season date phrases need roughly 95–100px to avoid excessive four-line fragmentation.
The yield column needs about 80–88px so ranges such as ৭.৮–৮.৪ stay on one line.
Crop names such as সরিষা (বাড়ি সরিষা-১৪) fit acceptably at 95px, so extra width there is not worth taking from মন্তব্য.
The remarks column needs roughly 235–255px to keep the table compact and prevent six-line prose cells.

tradeoffs: One could give crop names 105px and remarks 234px, as in r2C, for a slightly more comfortable row-header column; the cost is less breathing room for the longest prose. One could also widen the date columns for fewer wraps, but that makes the table taller by starving মন্তব্য.
uncertain: Exact Bengali glyph widths and browser line-breaking at the en dash may make the 80px yield column marginal for some values. Reasonable designers may disagree on whether r2C's extra crop-name width is worth the lost remarks width, and on whether r2A/r2B are merely inefficient rather than clearly faulty.

critique.good: All five columns are legible: the crop column at 100px keeps names to two lines, the date columns at 145/135 hold sowing and harvest windows in three lines without splitting words, and the remarks column is readable even when narrow. The paired 145/135 rhythm between বপন and কাটা reads well as a comparison block.
critique.problems: The table balloons to 878px with wildly uneven row heights (73, 154, 114, 134…). Rows 2 and 3 look like different tables. Column 4 at 65px wraps the yield value ৫.৮–/৬.৪ onto two lines and stacks its header into three cramped lines, so the shortest, most scannable datum becomes the fussiest cell.
critique.cause: মন্তব্য at 174px (153px of text) is too narrow for free prose, producing 7-line remark cells that dictate row height; meanwhile 280px is spent on the two date columns. Width is allocated against the reader's needs — remarks are the long-text column and got the third-largest share.

critique.good: The crop column is efficient and the date columns are airy — every sowing and harvest window sits comfortably in two to three lines, so the temporal pair is easy to compare at a glance.
critique.problems: By far the worst result: 1119px tall, remarks cells up to 9 lines, rows of 194/154/174px. The table no longer reads as rows at all — the eye loses the row unit between a two-line date cell and a nine-line comment. It also looks top-heavy and unbalanced: narrow date columns are wide, wide remarks are narrow.
critique.cause: মন্তব্য squeezed to 139px (118px of text) while বপন/কাটা were given 170/155 — roughly 70px of slack in the date columns that the remarks column desperately needed. The narrowest column holds the longest content, so height explodes.

critique.good: The most successful: compact 656px, remarks at 234px breathe (tallest cell only 5 lines), rows stay short and even-ish, and the table finally reads as a scannable schedule. Header wrapping is controlled and no words break.
critique.problems: The crop column at 85px (64px of text) is visibly pinched — 'সরিষা (বারি সরিষা-১৪)' and 'পাট (তোষা)' stack into three thin lines, and the longest unbreakable word is 61px inside a 64px box, an uncomfortable near-collision. Columns 2 and 3 at 125/115 are too tight for the date phrases, so they break into 3–4 lines and row 2 swells to 114px against 94px elsewhere; the unequal 125/115 also breaks the rhythm of the paired columns.
critique.cause: Remarks was funded almost entirely from the crop and date columns: 85px is below what the variety identifiers need, and 125/115 is below the one-line date width (231/209), so wrapping migrates from remarks into the date pair without actually shortening the table.

critique.good: The paired date columns are the widest and read as a balanced pair; crop labels stay intact and there are no mid-word splits. The table remains legible as a whole.
critique.problems: The yield column is a bottleneck: values such as ৭.৮–৬.৪ break across two lines, and the header stacks into three lines: ফলন / (টন/ / হেক্টর). Remarks are forced into six lines, making the table 777px tall and leaving the date columns with unused vertical space beside tall remark cells.
critique.cause: Col 4 at 60px leaves only 39px of text, less than the yield range needs. Col 5 at 200px is too narrow for the long remarks, while cols 2–3 at 132px each are overfed relative to their 2–3 line content.

critique.good: The crop column at 110px gives row labels more breathing room. The date columns are slightly differentiated in the right direction, 125/118, because col 2 is longer. The table is 20px shorter than r1A.
critique.problems: The yield column is still 60px, so the same numeric split and three-line header remain. Remarks still reach six lines. The date columns lost width to fund cols 1 and 5, so the schedule comparison is tighter without solving the main defect.
critique.cause: Col 4 was left unchanged at 60px. The extra 15px for col 1 and 6px for col 5 came from cols 2–3, so the budget moved sideways rather than fixing the numeric column.

critique.good: Best vertical rhythm: remarks at 223px reduce several rows to four lines and table height to 716px. Date columns remain readable, and crop labels stay intact.
critique.problems: Yield values still split and the header still stacks into three lines. Col 1 at 90px is the tightest, so parenthetical crop identifiers crowd the edge and can wrap awkwardly. The numeric outcome column looks visually weak compared with the remarks.
critique.cause: Col 4 is again only 60px, while the width that could have fixed it is spread into col 5 at 223px and the date columns. Col 1 is underfunded at 90px.

critique.good: Clear row anchors, a coherent paired sowing/harvest block at 112/105, compact yield column, and remarks as the widest column. Date phrases stay at three lines and there are no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: Rows are very tall, up to 134px, because remarks still runs to six lines. The schedule columns look relatively airy while the prose column is cramped. Crop labels at 100px all wrap, though that is not the main height driver.
critique.cause: Remarks gets only 217px (196px of text) against a 908px one-line need, so it sets row height. The 112/105 schedule widths are already above the threshold for three-line dates, so extra pixels there do not shorten rows; those pixels could go to remarks. The 100px crop column is also below the comfortable 105px that keeps short labels like পাট (তোষা) on one line.

critique.good: The most readable schedule: 120/110 gives the date windows the most room, keeps the paired columns related, and preserves all words intact.
critique.problems: Worst overall balance. Remarks at 209px is the narrowest and wraps to six lines, so the table is as tall as r2A despite the extra schedule width. The 95px crop column is cramped and weakens the row anchor.
critique.cause: Width is over-allocated to columns 2–3 beyond the three-line threshold, while column 5 is starved at 209px. Crop at 95px gives only 74px of text, below the comfortable width for bold crop labels; the long remarks column still controls every row height, so the schedule gain buys no vertical saving.

critique.good: Best balance so far. Remarks at 234px cuts the tallest cell to five lines and the table to 636px. Crop at 105px keeps row anchors strong and keeps short labels such as পাট (তোষা) on one line. The 100/95 schedule pair preserves a three-line rhythm, and yield values remain intact. No mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The first data row is 114px while the rest are 94px because its remark still runs to five lines. Remarks remains the tightest prose measure, and the yield header breaks awkwardly after টন/ rather than at the space.
critique.cause: At 234px the remarks text measure is 213px, just short of the roughly 238px needed to pull the longest remark from five lines to four, so the first row is an isolated taller row. The 85px yield column gives 64px of text, less than the 95px one-line header, so the header must break at the slash. The schedule columns are at a good three-line threshold, so narrowing them further risks four-line dates.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r3C.why: The comments have room to read, yield ranges stay on one line, and the rows remain compact. Sowing and harvest dates wrap frequently, though their similar widths support comparison.

ref_equal.why: The narrow comments column produces very tall rows and leaves large empty areas under the shorter fields. The equal widths give yield much more space than it needs.

ref_auto.why: Comments and dates have a workable balance, but several yield ranges break across lines and the yield header takes three lines, making that column harder to scan.

r1B.why: Sowing and harvest dates have useful space, but the yield column splits every range across lines. The narrower comments column also makes the rows noticeably taller.

r2C.why: Yield ranges stay intact and comments read comfortably. The similarly sized sowing and harvest columns preserve their relationship, though dates still wrap over several lines.

r3A.why: Comments are readable and yield ranges stay intact. The comparable date columns wrap often, and the crop names have slightly less room than in A or E.

raw.unsure: The three strongest layouts are very close; their small width differences offer different compromises between crop labels, dates and comments.

r2C.why: The remarks have comfortable line lengths, yield ranges stay intact, and the two date columns have similar weight. Crop names and several dates wrap over multiple lines, but rows remain easy to follow.

r3A.why: The wider remarks column reads well, yield ranges remain intact, and the date columns are balanced. The narrow crop and date columns create frequent wrapping.

ref_equal.why: Equal column widths leave the long remarks in a very narrow measure, making rows exceptionally tall and leaving large empty areas under the other cells.

ref_auto.why: Remarks and dates have useful space, but the narrow yield column splits several numeric ranges across lines and forces its header into three lines, impairing comparison.

r1B.why: Dates and crop names have room, but every yield range breaks across lines and the yield header is cramped. The narrower remarks column also makes rows taller.

r3C.why: Remarks are readable and yield ranges stay on one line. The crop and paired date columns remain comparable, though dates wrap frequently and the narrower harvest column produces some extra breaks.

raw.unsure: A and B are very close: A gives crop names slightly more room, while B gives remarks more room. Their relative benefit depends on whether readers prioritize scanning crop labels or reading notes.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
